name: happy
description:
Cyberint publishes alerts, not devices, so the import pivots each alert onto the domains it names in related_assets and emits one asset per domain carrying those alerts as findings. Proves the cookie-authenticated POST is made, that severity is mapped to a rank, that an alert with no id is skipped, that a related asset that is not a domain is ignored, and that two alerts naming the same domain land on one asset.

`namespaced_ids` is skipped because this integration violates it: the id is the domain with dots replaced by dashes and no tenant scope at all, so two Cyberint tenants that both watch example.com collide onto one asset. Reported as a defect with this batch.

Each domain's FIRST alert used to be attached twice -- build() seeded the list with `related_assets[domain] = [vuln]` and then appended the same vuln unconditionally, so shop.example.com came out with alert-0001, alert-0001, alert-0002 and portal.example.com with alert-0002 twice. That is fixed; the exact count is pinned by the duplicate-vulns scenario, which can bound it from above via the 99-child cap.

alerts.title: Exposed administrative interface
alerts.description: An administrative interface is reachable from the public internet.
alerts.recommendation: Restrict the interface to an allowlisted network.
